purpose: Test whether the Design Council skill adds single-turn outcome value beyond a competent frozen Design Thinking prompt without the plugin.

intervention.treatment: Repository-local Design Council skill frozen before the first model call.
intervention.control: No plugin, state, Human Models, Council protocols, or modular references; the same raw user prompt was preceded by one frozen competent Design Thinking instruction.

reporting_hierarchy.primary_question: Does Design Council produce a practically meaningful single-turn outcome-quality benefit over a competent prompt-only Design Thinking session?
reporting_hierarchy.basis: The observed treatment-control difference was -1.547619 points and the 95% case-bootstrap interval [-4.642857, 1.785714] crossed zero; the run therefore established neither a treatment advantage nor a reliable control advantage.
reporting_hierarchy.resource_note: Token use is a secondary optimization descriptor and does not determine the outcome-quality verdict. Here it reinforces, but does not cause, the conclusion that this run established no incremental benefit.

outcome_construct_profile.note: These groups overlap and are diagnostic means, not independent validated psychometric subscales.

interpretation: This internal Codex run does not establish that the beta3 Design Council snapshot improves a competent one-shot Design Thinking prompt. The point estimate slightly favored the prompt-only control, but the interval crossed zero. Design Council improved methodological rigor, task fit, and appropriate-scope handling, while the prompt-only control was stronger on breadth/non-obviousness, evidence calibration, and communication efficiency. The raw-prompt comparison remains positive evidence against an unassisted session; it must not be presented as proof of incremental value beyond competent prompt engineering.
limitations: The product team authored the prompt corpus, control instruction, and rubrics.
The judge was a model, not an independent human panel.
Candidate wording could reveal Design Council terminology even though arm labels were blind.
Seven of 24 pairs changed winner across counterbalanced judge presentations.
Two candidate responses exceeded the shared 900-word cap.
Bundled host-runtime capabilities remained a shared environmental boundary.

This was a single-turn Codex study and cannot measure the plugin's proposed longitudinal value from persistent project memory, evidence-driven iteration, facilitated participation, or multi-cycle Council work.
The frozen treatment snapshot was captured from a dirty beta3 working tree; later refinements require a new frozen run rather than being inferred from this result.
Held-out external prompts and independent human raters are required before a public efficacy claim.
No authenticated native Claude study was run, so no Claude efficacy claim is made.
Token ratios are resource descriptors, not monetary ROI and not a substitute for outcome quality.
next_validation: Run scripted multi-turn trajectories that score frame changes, evidence integration, divergence, experiment information gain, and backward iteration.
Use held-out prompts contributed by people who did not author the product or benchmark.
Conduct blind human paired review with quality ratings locked before resource use is shown.
Repeat the within-platform comparison in an authenticated native Claude Code runtime.
